intent: Practice counting back on a number line where each hop corresponds to moving to the next number rather than counting the start number

data.title: Hop Back on the Number Line
data.description: Learn how to subtract numbers within 20 by counting back on a number line.

challenges.instruction: Put your finger on the number 8, and hop back 2 spaces to the left to see where you land!
challenges.hint: Count the hops one by one as you move 2 spaces to the left from 8.

challenges.instruction: Let us try another jump! Start at 5 on the number line and hop backward 4 spaces to the left.
challenges.hint: Put your finger on 5 and carefully count 4 individual hops to the left.

challenges.instruction: Put your frog on the number 16. Now, hop backward 2 spaces to the left!
challenges.hint: Count each hop backward one by one: 1... 2...

challenges.instruction: Put your finger on 18, and get ready to hop backward 4 spaces to see where you land!
challenges.hint: Follow the drawn jump arc and count each hop backward one by one as you go.

judgement.reasoning: The activity uses the exact same number-line representation and simply prompts the student to make jumps (e.g., hop back 2 from 8), but with showJumpArc: true. While focusing on hops addresses moving spaces, it doesn't offer a fundamentally new perspective or isolate the starting count vs hop mismatch any better than the original activity, staying on the same tool.
judgement.verdict: This keeps the student on the same tool without effectively highlighting why counting the starting point is incorrect.
